chunks: First: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the son of a paternal aunt and the son of a maternal aunt. He said: The son of the maternal aunt receives one-sixth, and the son of the paternal aunt receives the remainder.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report indicates that when a maternal sister and a paternal sister are present, the maternal sister is given one-sixth by name, and the paternal sister is given one-half by name, and the remainder is returned to her, because her daughter only takes what she would have taken if she were alive, as she approaches [the deceased] through her and takes the share of whom she approaches through. This is contrary to what some of our companions hold regarding the obligation of return to both of them, because that is an error according to the requirement of this text.

Second: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

He said: I asked him about the son of a paternal uncle and the son of a maternal uncle. He said: The son of the maternal uncle receives one-sixth, and whatever remains is for the son of the paternal uncle.

Third: As for what al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Miskeen, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'The daughters of a brother and the son of a brother.' He said: 'The wealth is for the son of the brother.' I said, 'Their kinship is one.' He said: 'The blood money is upon them, and there is nothing upon the women.' This report is consistent with the general public, but we do not act upon it due to the consensus of the true sect on acting contrary to it.

Because we have clarified that when the kinship is equal, they share in the inheritance, whether males or females, and each takes the share of whom he approaches through. It is also possible that the report is specific to the son of a brother when he is from both father and mother, and the daughters of a brother from the father's side. If that is the case, then they are not entitled to anything, because if their father were alive with the brother from father and mother, he would have nothing in any case.

key_terms.العاقلة: Clan/kinship group responsible for blood money

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed between paternal and maternal cousins in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the inheritance shares of cousins (ibn al-akh) by distinguishing between paternal and maternal lines, establishing that the maternal cousin receives a fixed one-sixth while the paternal cousin takes the remainder. It highlights the Shia scholarly debate on whether this reflects a specific rule for mixed-lineage cousins or a general principle where maternal relatives are excluded in favor of paternal ones, contrasting with the Sunni view of equal sharing among equal kin. The text further notes that while some reports align with the general public (al-‘ammah), Shia jurists prioritize the consensus (ijma’) of their school, which favors equal distribution among cousins of the same degree of kinship.
